title: Delayed Versus Early Salvage Radiotherapy for Low-Risk Biochemical Recurrence After Prostatectomy
official: Phase III Trial for Economic Evaluation of Delayed Salvage Radiotherapy (SRT) for Prostate Cancer in Men With EAU Low-risk Biochemical Recurrence and Negative PSMA PET Results (DIPPER-ME)
summary:
Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels may increase after radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer, indicating a biochemical recurrence of the disease. Salvage radiotherapy is commonly used in this situation, but it may cause side effects that can affect patients' quality of life. For patients with a lower risk of disease progression and a negative PSMA PET scan, it is uncertain whether radiotherapy should be started early or whether it can be safely delayed.

This phase III randomized study will compare two management strategies in patients with low-risk biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy: early salvage radiotherapy initiated at a PSA level of 0.2 ng/mL or higher, and delayed salvage radiotherapy initiated at a PSA level of 0.5 ng/mL or higher. A total of 156 participants will be enrolled.

In addition to evaluating clinical outcomes, the study will assess healthcare costs and quality of life associated with both strategies. Quality of life will be measured using patient-reported outcomes, and healthcare resource utilization will be collected throughout the study and linked with national healthcare data sources. The study aims to determine whether delaying salvage radiotherapy can reduce treatment burden, improve quality of life, and optimize healthcare resource use while maintaining clinical outcomes comparable to those achieved with early radiotherapy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Men ≥ 18 years old with pathological diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the prostate cancer previously treated with radical prostatectomy.
* Performance Status (PS) 0-1.
* PSA undetectable (\<0.10 ng/mL) after prostatectomy.
* Post prostatectomy biochemical recurrence (PSA 0.15 ng/mL \< 0.5 ng/mL) with two documented consecutive PSA increases at least 14 days apart.
* Low-risk biochemical recurrence according to EAU guidelines: Gleason Score (GS) ≤ 4+3 or ISUP group ≤ 3 AND PSA doubling time (PSADT) \> 12 months, based on the last three PSA values ≥ 0.1 ng/mL.
* No prior treatment for this biochemical recurrence.
* No evidence of locally recurrent or metastatic disease according to PSMA PET/CT
* Patient able to complete patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs).
* Presence of a designated caregiver willing to complete the caregiver quality-of-life questionnaires required by the study
* Agreement to use effective contraception for men and their partners of childbearing potential
* Affiliation to a national insurance scheme (as required by national regulations).
* Patient informed and having signed written informed consent.
* Patients willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures as specified in the protocol.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of a positive PSMA PET scan in the context of biochemical recurrence (local recurrence, regional lymph node metastasis, or distant metastasis).
* Prior pelvic radiotherapy that would interfere with the study radiotherapy.
* Contraindications to radiotherapy (including active inflammatory bowel disease).
* Ongoing androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) or systemic therapy for biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer.
* Bilateral orchiectomy.
* Positive regional lymph node disease (pN1) at radical prostatectomy.
* History of cancer within 3 years prior to study entry, other than adequately treated cutaneous basal cell carcinoma or non-muscle-invasive bladder carcinoma.
* Concomitant disease, including severe infection, that could compromise the patient's ability to safely comply with the procedures described in this protocol.
* Participation in other clinical trials involving experimental treatments for prostate cancer or any other disease.
* Individuals deprived of liberty or under legal protection measures (guardianship or trusteeship).
* Inability to comply with study follow-up for geographic, social, or psychological reasons.
